items.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003
items.q: you’d get all the Glenn Miller stuff, like “In the Mood,” “Little Brown Jug” and all that

ctx.x: Yeah. And what else would have been on your song list? Ellington stuff?

Oh well, sure. You played, back then you couldn’t play in a band, a horn, unless you were just jamming in a club, without being able to read music. Because they passed out what they called stock arrangements. Now they had these stock arrangements where you’d get all the Glenn Miller stuff, like “In the Mood,” “Little Brown Jug” and all that; the Tommy Dorsey stuff; Benny Goodman stuff. And you played all that because that was the popular stuff on the radio and that’s what people expected to dance to when you…
Would there have been a singer?
